subject: SLA baseline, monthly remedy schedule & regional maintenance carveout
messages:
From: Thomas Hale <thomas.hale@auroratech.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@auroratech.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: SLA baseline, monthly remedy schedule & regional maintenance carveout

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Our legal and ops teams reviewed the standard SLA template you shared. A few items are blockers for AuroraTech before procurement can sign:

- The baseline uptime in the template (99.95%) is fine, but we need an explicit ramp for the first 90 days of production (we expect a higher error surface during warm-up). We’d like credits to be smoothed across the ramp window rather than applied month-by-month.
- Regional maintenance carveout: Aurora runs peak trading in EU business hours. We need a committed weekly maintenance window (up to 3 hours) for EU-region upgrades with 72 hours’ notice and no credit trigger inside that window.
- Latency SLOs: your template references p95 latency targets but no concrete remediation bands for p99 spikes; we need clearer language.

Attached are our redlines (AuroraTech_SLA_Redlines_v2.pdf). Can Redwood propose a concrete compromise on ramped credit smoothing and a maintenance carveout that preserves our peak windows?

Best,
Thomas Hale
Director of Platform Ops
AuroraTech

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: SLA baseline, monthly remedy schedule & regional maintenance carveout

Hi Thomas —

Appreciate the clear redlines and context. I’ve looped in Laura (legal) and Rishi (SRE) to work through the ramp and carveout mechanics. High level answers up-front:

- We can do a 90-day ramp with a smoothing proposal (apply remedy liability as a trailing 90-day rolling window instead of per calendar month) — need to align on exact cap.
- Weekly maintenance carveout for EU region is doable with guardrails (advance notice, maximum cumulative monthly outage cap).
- We’ll propose specific p99 remediation bands; our default is to tie monetary remedy to availability, and offer service credits for repeat p99 latency regressions as an alternative remediation path.

Next steps from our side: Laura will propose contract language and cap levels; Rishi will propose maintenance notice/process and latency band definitions. Can Aurora confirm the preferred maintenance window days/times (UTC) and whether a single weekly window is sufficient vs. two smaller windows?

Thanks — I’ll consolidate and send a proposed compromise by tomorrow EOD.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Head of GTM Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Thomas Hale <thomas.hale@auroratech.com>, Legal Ops <legal@auroratech.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 14:29:00 -0400
Subject: Re: SLA baseline, monthly remedy schedule & regional maintenance carveout

Thomas / Aurora team —

Thanks for sending the redlines. I took a first pass at language that we think balances operational flexibility with predictable remedy exposure. Key points in the attached markup:

- 90-day ramp: remedies calculated on a trailing 90-day weighted average. Credits are still issued monthly but are capped in any calendar month at 10% of the monthly bill during the ramp period (this prevents front-loading while acknowledging higher initial risk).
- Maintenance carveout: single weekly 3-hour window per region permitted with 72-hour notice; carveout does not apply to emergency maintenance required to remediate security incidents. The aggregate maintenance carveout cannot exceed 6 hours in any calendar month.
- Latency: add a p99 remediation band. If p99 exceeds threshold more than twice in a 30-day window, customer can elect a credit equal to X% of monthly spend or request a technical remediation plan.

I’m attaching the proposed compromise as a short spreadsheet with cap examples (redwood-proposed-compromise.xlsx). If Aurora is comfortable with the 10% cap during ramp, we can convert to contract text and circulate a tracked changes PDF.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-proposed-compromise.xlsx (spreadsheet - remedy cap examples)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Thomas Hale <thomas.hale@auroratech.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 17:42:00 -0400
Subject: Proposed operational compromise — weekly maintenance carveout + ramp smoothing

Thomas —

Thanks again for the detailed ask. Operationally we can accept Aurora’s request with the following compromise (summary below; contract text to follow from Laura):

1) Ramp & smoothing
- 90-day onboarding ramp. Remedies are calculated using a trailing 90-day weighted average of availability.
- During ramp, monthly credit issuance is capped at 10% of that month’s invoice. Any amount above the cap is tracked and eligible for payout in subsequent months within the same trailing 90-day window (so customer sees smoothing rather than month-to-month volatility).

2) Weekly maintenance carveout (EU region)
- Single weekly window up to 3 hours (customer to nominate preferred weekday/time in UTC).
- 72 hours’ advance notice required for planned maintenance.
- Carveout excluded from remedies except where maintenance exceeds 3 hours or aggregate monthly carveout >6 hours — in that case time beyond the allowance will count against availability and may trigger credits.
- Emergency security maintenance: immediate patching allowed; such events will be logged and reviewed — not eligible for carveout if the event was caused by Redwood negligence.

3) Latency remediation band
- Add p99 remediation: if p99 exceeds agreed threshold on more than 2 non-consecutive days within any 30-day window, Aurora may request a technical remediation plan. Repeated p99 regressions (3+ instances) trigger an optional credit equal to 5% of monthly spend for that month.

Next steps / asks from Aurora:
- Confirm preferred EU weekly maintenance window (weekday + UTC start time).
- Confirm acceptance of the 10% monthly cap during the 90-day ramp.
- If accepted, Laura will prepare tracked contract language for signature.

If it helps, Marissa can run a short example on Aurora’s projected monthly spend to show how smoothing behaves across months.

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Site Reliability Engineering, Redwood Inference
